author: Swinhoe, 1861
summary: 4월과 10월에 우리나라를 지나가는 나그네새로, 논이나 호수 습지의 갈대밭, 풀밭에서 지낸다. 홀로 또는 2~3마리의 작은 무리로 다닌다. 연체동물, 모족류, 곤충, 갑각류, 물고기와 식물 열매를 먹는다. 땅 위에 접시 모양 둥지를 짓고 알 4개를 낳는다.

points.en: outer tail feathers with two bars near the tip

points.ko: 끝에 넓은 붉은 갈색 띠가 있는 가운데 꼬리깃
points.en: broad central tail feathers with a wide rufous-brown tip band

similar.how: 바깥꼬리깃이 그리 가늘지 않고 끝에 가로무늬가 2개 있다. 꼬리깃이 20장이고 바깥 5~7장만 바늘꼬리이며, 가운데 5~6장은 폭이 넓고 끝에 넓은 붉은 갈색 띠가 있다.

art.subject: Swinhoe's Snipe (Gallinago megala), adult (sexes alike, same plumage in spring and autumn), as seen at Korean paddy and marsh edges in April-May and August-October: crown blackish-brown with a buff central stripe; broad buff supercilium which, in front of the eye, is wider than the dark eye-stripe; dark cheek bar; upperparts blackish-brown with buff and rufous bars and pale buff mantle lines, the scapulars with narrower, more even buff fringes so the back looks less boldly striped than a Common Snipe's; neck and breast buffy-brown mottled and barred dark; flanks densely barred dark brown; belly white; bill long and straight, greyish-brown at the base with a dark tip; dark eye; legs dull olive-yellow to greenish-yellow.
art.pose: standing in reeds at the edge of a marsh, side view
art.scene: Korean rice fields beside a reedy lake marsh in April or October; no people, buildings or text
views: tail detail from above, fully spread: about 20 feathers; broad central feathers black at the base with a wide rufous-brown band near the tip; the outer five to seven pairs progressively narrower towards the outside but not needle-thin, whitish-buff crossed by dark bars near the tip

adult, side view standing in grass with the tail slightly fanned: heavy body, long straight bill, buff supercilium wider than the eye-stripe in front of the eye, blackish-brown upperparts edged buff, barred flanks, white belly, rufous-brown band near the tail tip, greenish-yellow legs
art.build: Heavy-bodied snipe, a little larger and bulkier than Common Snipe and smaller than a feral pigeon, with a larger, squarer head, thicker neck and stout legs; crouching, horizontal stance. Bill straight and long (about twice the head length), thick at the base. Legs fairly short, dull greenish-yellow, thicker than in Common Snipe. Tail of about 20 feathers: the central ones broad, black at the base with a wide rufous-brown band near the tip; the outer five to seven pairs become narrower towards the outside but stay vane-like, not pin-thin, and are pale with dark bars. In flight no white trailing edge to the wing and a dark, densely barred underwing.
avoid: Do not paint the outer tail feathers as needle-thin pins - that is Pin-tailed Snipe (Gallinago stenura); here they are narrow but still vane-like.
Do not paint a bold white trailing edge to the wing or white bars on the underwing - those are Common Snipe features.
Do not curve the bill or shorten it below about twice the head length.
Do not paint long or bright yellow-orange legs.
